answer: Submissions that land within 37 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The knoll detector writes to vault, and plume shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 242 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 38 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
